sentences.text: For Respondent(s) : Mr. Divyesh Maheshwari Mr. Babu Lal Nasuna, PP HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SAMEER JAIN Order 15/07/2024 1.

This petition under Section 482 Cr. P.C. is filed with a prayer to quash the FIR No. 352/2018 registered at Mahila Police Station District Kota, for offences under Sections 498A, 406 of IPC, on the basis of compromise effectuated between the parties herein, in respect of their inter-se dispute.
2. Learned counsel for the parties have submitted that the parties want to put a quietus to the matter, which pertains to an inter se dispute, between the parties.

In pursuance of the orders dated 02.04.2024 and 24.05.2024, the learned counsel for the petitioner has presented Demand Drafts No.829738 dated 15.05.2024 worth Rs. 99,00,000/-, and Demand Draft No.829741 dated 16.05.2024 worth Rs. 12,00,000/-.
The said Demand Drafts were handed over to Mr. Divyesh Maheshwari on behalf of the non-petitioners, before this Court.
It is submitted by both the parties that they are in agreement to honor the consensus encapsulated in the 'Memorandum of Understanding'.

Further, both the parties have submitted that they are eager to file an application under Section 13B of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 before the concerned Family Court as the terms of the compromise deed are complied with.

[2024:RJ-JP:29555] (3 of 3) [CRLMP-8223/2018]
3. Learned counsel for both the parties have further submitted that the parties without any coercion or influence have entered into a compromise.
Hence, both the parties have jointly agreed for quashing the impugned FIR and any further proceedings, arising therefrom.

4. Heard and considered.
5.

At this juncture, this Court deems it appropriate to place reliance upon the dictum of the Hon'ble Apex Court enunciated in Jasmair Singh Vs. State of Haryana [(2022) 9 SCC 73] and Gian Singh Vs.
State of Punjab [(2012) 10 SCC 303], wherein, it was held that a case was eminently suitable to be considered for exercise of jurisdiction under Section 482 Cr.PC for quashing of criminal proceedings, if the parties have buried the hatchet and decided to give quietus to the proceedings,
which were lodged inter se against one another.

entities.text: Jasmair Singh Vs. State of Haryana [(2022) 9 SCC 73]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text:
Gian Singh Vs.
State of Punjab [(2012) 10 SCC 303]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
5. In view of the said legal position, laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in aforementioned cases,
and considering the fact that the dispute deals in personam and has amicably been settled between/by the parties, this Court deems it appropriate to allow the present misc. Petition.
The compromise is taken on record.

6. Considering the aforementioned, the present criminal miscellaneous petition is disposed of and the FIR No. 352/2018 registered at Mahila Police Station District Kota, with all consequential proceedings, is hereby quashed and set aside.
(SAMEER JAIN),J JKP/482 Powered by TCPDF (www.tcpdf.org)
